title: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central Pricing: 2026
summary: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central pricing ranges from $8 to $110 per user monthly. Right tier assignments for each role prevent overspending.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is there a free trial of Business Central?


Yes, Microsoft offers a time-limited trial you can start from its own site, and it's worth using to learn the screens.


Treat it as a look at the product, not a rehearsal of your setup. It runs on sample data, so you learn nothing about how your items, customers and bank feeds will behave.


However well a trial goes, it says little about what implementation will cost.


### Can I mix Business Central plans in one company?


Not freely. Essentials and Premium can't be mixed within one environment, so one person who needs Premium features moves everyone onto Premium pricing.


Lighter user types, such as Team Members, can sit alongside either plan, and that's where the savings are. Before you price the whole team at the top rate, count how many people only approve, view or enter time.


### Does Business Central pricing include Microsoft 365 or Power Platform?


No. Microsoft 365 (Outlook, Excel, Teams) is a separate subscription, and Business Central works with it but doesn't bundle it. Power Platform is partly covered: your licence lets you build apps and automations that extend Business Central itself.


When something reaches into other systems or other data, it usually needs its own Power Platform licence. If your plan depends on automation, ask your partner in writing which side of that line each integration falls on.


### How often does Microsoft change Business Central prices?


There's no fixed schedule. Microsoft announces changes ahead of time, and the most recent increase raised both per-user plans. That's why a quote needs an end date and a statement of what happens at renewal.


Billing terms matter here too. Whether you pay monthly or commit annually changes how exposed you are to a rise, so confirm which one your quote assumes.


Ask for storage allowances and limits on connecting other software in writing, rather than assuming they're the same on every plan: they also vary by how you license.


### Can I buy Business Central without a partner?


Yes. Microsoft sells licences directly, and you can buy and assign them yourself.


The licence is only the easy part, though. Setting up your chart of accounts, moving your old data and training staff is where most of the money goes, and a self-service purchase leaves all of it to you.


For a very small business with simple books and someone patient enough to learn the system, buying direct can make sense. For anyone else, skipping the partner moves the cost to a later and less predictable place, usually in lost staff time and corrections.
